title: Skin Lesion Classification Using Convolutional Neural Network With Novel Regularizer
authors: M. A. Albahar
dataset_size: 23,906 images (ISIC Archive; 8,000 subset evaluated: 5,600 train, 2,400 val)
model_architecture: Constructed a 2-layer convolutional network embedded with a novel weight regularizer (penalty hyperparameter lambda = 0.02), coupled with max pooling, dropout, a 128-neuron dense layer, and softmax output.
preprocessing: Applied power-law transformation to standardize 300x300x3 dermoscopic images, balancing illumination differences and highlighting subtle boundary gradations prior to convolution.
classification_task: Binary skin lesion classification (Malignant Melanoma vs. Benign Nevus)
main_results: Accuracy: 97.49%, AUC (Nevus vs Mel): 0.77, AUC (SK vs BCC): 0.93, AUC (SK vs Mel): 0.85
main_contribution: Yes. The novel regularizer successfully stabilized weight trajectories during 100 training epochs, achieving an average validation weighted accuracy of 97.49% and preventing divergence on fine-grained lesion classes. Designed: Regularized & Lightweight CNNs
limitations: The binary pairwise formulation cannot holistically evaluate complex multi-class differential diagnoses, and the lack of external prospective multi-center testing limits generalizability.
future_work: How can the weight regularizer be generalized to unified multi-class differential diagnosis without loss of per-class sensitivity?; How does the model perform prospectively across diverse patient phototypes in multi-center clinical trials?
research_gaps: Fine-grained morphological overlaps between benign and malignant skin lesions cause catastrophic overfitting in traditional unregularized deep CNNs.
relevance_to_my_study: Directly informs CNN transfer learning selection, layer fine-tuning strategies, and comparative architectural benchmarking for dermoscopic feature extraction.

title: Region-of-Interest Based Transfer Learning Assisted Framework for Skin Cancer Detection
authors: R. Ashraf; S. Afzal; A. U. Rehman; S. Gul; J. Baber; M. Bakhtyar; I. Mehmood; O. -Y. Song; M. Maqsood
dataset_size: DermIS (705 images: 448 benign, 257 melanoma); DermQuest (667 images: 434 nevus, 233 melanoma)
model_architecture: Implemented improved k-means clustering to segment lesion borders, followed by ROI cropping and offline data augmentation (rotations, flips, zooming, contrast adjustments).
preprocessing: Standard resizing to input resolution and pixel normalization
augmentation: random rotations, flipping, zooming, and contrast adjustments
classification_task: Binary skin lesion classification (Malignant Melanoma vs. Benign Nevus)
main_results: Accuracy (DermIS): 97.9%, Sensitivity: 96.3%, Specificity: 98.7%, AUC (DermIS): 0.97, Accuracy (DermQuest): 97.4%, AUC (DermQuest): 0.96
main_contribution: Yes. Eliminating healthy skin artifacts allowed feature extraction networks to focus exclusively on lesion texture, boosting accuracy to 97.9% on DermIS and 97.4% on DermQuest. Designed: ROI Localization & Transfer Learning
limitations: k-means clustering degrades in the presence of severe hair occlusion and diffuse, poorly demarcated lesion margins, leading to border over-clipping or under-segmentation.
future_work: Can automated deep semantic segmentation replace k-means to eliminate manual tuning in the presence of dense hair?; Can the framework scale to multi-class classification beyond binary melanoma vs. nevus distinction?
research_gaps: Surrounding healthy skin, lighting variations, and hair artifacts introduce confounding background noise when deep networks process full unsegmented dermoscopic images.
relevance_to_my_study: Directly informs CNN transfer learning selection, layer fine-tuning strategies, and comparative architectural benchmarking for dermoscopic feature extraction.

title: An Interpretable Skin Cancer Classification Using Optimized Convolutional Neural Network for a Smart Healthcare System
authors: K. Mridha; M. M. Uddin; J. Shin; S. Khadka; M. F. Mridha
model_architecture: Trained a custom CNN with batch normalization, max pooling, and dropout across systematic combinations of optimizers and activation functions.
augmentation: random rotations, zooms, shear transformations, and flips
main_results: Accuracy: 82.0%, Specificity: 94.17%, Sensitivity: 82.0%, Loss Accuracy: 0.47%
main_contribution: The custom CNN achieved peak overall accuracy of 82.0% and specificity of 94.17% with Adam optimizer and Swish/ReLU activations, with a loss accuracy of 0.47%. Designed: Explainable AI (XAI) & Mobile Healthcare
limitations: Successfully validated end-to-end mobile execution with near real-time inference latency suitable for decentralized point-of-care screening.
future_work: How can synthetic metric oversampling or cost-sensitive losses improve minority class sensitivity in mobile models?; What is the diagnostic accuracy of the Android application when tested prospectively in multi-ethnic outpatient clinics?
research_gaps: Deep learning CAD systems act as 'black boxes', lacking visual transparency and suffering from severe performance drops on underrepresented minority classes in multi-class dermatological screening.
relevance_to_my_study: Directly utilizes HAM10000 / ISIC 2018 benchmark. Provides baseline architecture, class-imbalance evidence (minority classes df/vasc/akiec), and metrics for 7-class classification.

title: Automatic Skin Cancer Detection in Dermoscopy Images Based on Ensemble Lightweight Deep Learning Network
authors: L. Wei; K. Ding; H. Hu
dataset_size: ISBI 2016 (900 train, 379 test), ISBI 2017 Challenge Dataset
model_architecture: Designed a parameter-efficient ensemble using lightweight CNN feature extractors, a lightweight U-Net segmentation module, and a fine-grained discrimination network.
preprocessing: Standard resizing to input resolution and pixel normalization
classification_task: Binary skin lesion classification (Malignant Melanoma vs. Benign Nevus)
main_results: Accuracy: 87.3%, AUC: 0.886, Sensitivity: 83.2%, Specificity: 89.1%, Average Precision: 0.732
main_contribution: Yes. The framework achieved an accuracy of 87.3% and an AUC of 0.886 on ISBI 2016 with orders-of-magnitude fewer parameters than standard heavyweight baselines. Designed: Lightweight Networks & Ensemble Learning
limitations: Performance modestly degraded on lesions with fuzzy, diffuse boundaries, and training multiple lightweight networks sequentially introduced non-negligible training time overhead.
future_work: Can pair-based lightweight feature discrimination scale effectively to 8-class multi-category classification?; Can knowledge distillation compress the lightweight ensemble into a single ultra-compact inference model?
research_gaps: High computational complexity and massive parameter counts prevent deployment of state-of-the-art deep networks on resource-constrained clinical workstations and edge devices.
relevance_to_my_study: Directly informs CNN transfer learning selection, layer fine-tuning strategies, and comparative architectural benchmarking for dermoscopic feature extraction.

title: DeepSkin: A Deep Learning Approach for Skin Cancer Classification
authors: H. L. Gururaj; N. Manju; A. Nagarjun; V. N. M. Aradhya; F. Flammini
model_architecture: Architected DeepSkin with residual skip connections to preserve low-level textural gradients, benchmarked comparatively against VGG-16, ResNet-50, and MobileNet.
augmentation: procedures including random rotations, horizontal flipping, zooming, and brightness adjustments to combat class distribution skewness
main_results: Accuracy: 88.0%, Sensitivity: 86.2%, Specificity: 85.0%, Precision: 86.4%
main_contribution: DeepSkin achieved 88.0% overall accuracy, outperforming several heavier pre-trained models while maintaining architectural simplicity and compact parameterization. Designed: Residual Custom Architectures & Multi-Class Screening
limitations: Identified lack of hardware edge-profiling (FPS, RAM consumption) and absence of multi-ethnic clinical validation cohorts as critical deployment gaps.
future_work: How can attention gates be added to DeepSkin to resolve confusion between benign keratosis and melanoma?; What is the inference latency of DeepSkin on embedded microcontroller and edge-TPU hardware?
research_gaps: Existing CAD systems suffer from accuracy degradation in multi-class classification and require heavy pre-trained backbones that struggle with class-imbalanced dermoscopic archives.
relevance_to_my_study: Directly utilizes HAM10000 / ISIC 2018 benchmark. Provides baseline architecture, class-imbalance evidence (minority classes df/vasc/akiec), and metrics for 7-class classification.

authors: A. Naeem; M. S. Farooq; A. Khelifi; A. Abid
model_architecture: Conducted a systematic literature review following the Kitchenham protocol across IEEE, Springer, Elsevier, ACM, ScienceDirect, and Medline from 2014 to 2020.

limitations: Identified 3 major gaps: (1) lack of prospective multi-center clinical validation, (2) failure to integrate clinical demographic metadata, and (3) vulnerability to adversarial artifacts and hair occlusions.

relevance_to_my_study: Directly utilizes HAM10000 / ISIC 2018 benchmark. Provides baseline architecture, class-imbalance evidence (minority classes df/vasc/akiec), and metrics for 7-class classification.

datasets: ISIC Archive Curated Balanced Dataset (2,800 images: 1,400 benign, 1,400 malignant)
dataset_size: 2,800 curated images from ISIC (1,400 benign, 1,400 malignant)

research_gaps: Subtle chromatic and textural similarities between benign and malignant lesions yield high false-positive rates in single-model CAD systems.
relevance_to_my_study: Directly informs CNN transfer learning selection, layer fine-tuning strategies, and comparative architectural benchmarking for dermoscopic feature extraction.

title: Deep Clustering via Center-Oriented Margin Free-Triplet Loss for Skin Lesion Detection in Highly Imbalanced Datasets
authors: Ş. Öztürk; T. Çukur

relevance_to_my_study: Directly utilizes HAM10000 / ISIC 2018 benchmark. Provides baseline architecture, class-imbalance evidence (minority classes df/vasc/akiec), and metrics for 7-class classification.

title: Classification for Dermoscopy Images Using Convolutional Neural Networks Based on the Ensemble of Individual Advantage and Group Decision
authors: A. Gong; X. Yao; W. Lin
dataset_size: ISIC 2017 Challenge Dataset, ISIC 2018 Challenge Task 3
model_architecture: Constructed an ensemble framework that measures each model's class-specific diagnostic advantage on validation splits, assigning priority votes accordingly.
preprocessing: Standard resizing to input resolution and pixel normalization
main_results: Accuracy: 92.8%, Sensitivity: 91.5%, Specificity: 94.3%, AUC: 0.956
main_contribution: Yes. Group decision voting based on individual architectural advantages achieved 92.8% multiclass accuracy on ISIC 2018, outperforming uniform voting ensembles. Designed: Architectural Advantage Mining & Group Decision
limitations: Maintaining three distinct deep backbones substantially increases memory consumption and deployment complexity, with noticeable representation overlap across layers.
future_work: Can reinforcement learning dynamically select which single backbone to execute per image to avoid running all models concurrently?; How does individual advantage voting perform when expanding to 10+ rare dermatological categories?
research_gaps: Individual deep learning models possess unique diagnostic strengths on specific lesion sub-types but suffer from blind spots on others, which uniform averaging ensembles fail to leverage.
relevance_to_my_study: Directly utilizes HAM10000 / ISIC 2018 benchmark. Provides baseline architecture, class-imbalance evidence (minority classes df/vasc/akiec), and metrics for 7-class classification.

title: Pipelined Structure in the Classification of Skin Lesions Based on Alexnet CNN and SVM Model With Bi-Sectional Texture Features
authors: V. S. S. B. T. Sathvika; N. Anmisha; V. Thanmayi; M. Suchetha; D. E. Dhas; S. Sehastrajit; S. N. Aakur
model_architecture: Partitioned lesions geometrically along principal axes and extracted bi-sectional Gray-Level Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM) and statistical texture descriptors.
preprocessing: Standard resizing to input resolution and pixel normalization
main_results: Accuracy: 94.6%, Sensitivity: 93.8%, Specificity: 95.2%, F1-Score: 94.1%
main_contribution: Yes. Bi-sectional feature analysis explicitly captured morphological and textural asymmetry, providing discriminative cues that mirrored clinical ABCD criteria. Designed: Hybrid Deep Features & Handcrafted Textures
limitations: Fixed bi-sectional geometric partitioning fails on multi-lobed and non-convex lesions, and decoupling feature extraction from SVM training prevents end-to-end gradient updates.
future_work: Can differentiable geometric slicing layers enable end-to-end training of bi-sectional networks without separate SVM stages?; How does bi-sectional analysis perform on non-dermoscopic smartphone photos where lesion borders are ill-defined?
research_gaps: Deep features from standard CNNs often ignore geometric asymmetry and bi-sectional textural differences that dermatologists explicitly use in the ABCD criteria.
relevance_to_my_study: Directly utilizes HAM10000 / ISIC 2018 benchmark. Provides baseline architecture, class-imbalance evidence (minority classes df/vasc/akiec), and metrics for 7-class classification.

title: Improved Segmentation Model for Melanoma Lesion Detection Using Normalized Cross-Correlation-Based k-Means Clustering
authors: M. I. Faizi; S. M. Adnan
dataset_size: 200 dermoscopic images (PH2: 80 common nevi, 80 atypical nevi, 40 melanomas)
model_architecture: Formulated an improved k-means algorithm that uses Normalized Cross-Correlation as its similarity metric rather than standard Euclidean distance, matching template pigment distributions.
main_results: Segmentation Accuracy (PH2): 96.8%, Dice Coefficient: 93.4%, Jaccard Index: 87.9%
main_contribution: Yes. NCC-based k-means achieved an outstanding segmentation accuracy of 96.8% and a Dice coefficient of 93.4% on the PH2 benchmark. Designed: Lesion Segmentation & Normalized Cross-Correlation
limitations: NCC calculation is computationally more intensive than Euclidean distance, increasing per-image segmentation latency on ultra-high-resolution dermoscopic images.
future_work: Can GPU-accelerated FFTs speed up NCC template calculations for real-time mobile segmentation?; How does NCC k-means compare to modern deep transformer segmentation models like SegFormer?
research_gaps: Standard clustering algorithms (standard k-means, Otsu) are easily corrupted by non-uniform skin pigmentation, lighting gradients, and hair artifacts during boundary segmentation.
relevance_to_my_study: Provides comparative benchmark context on artifact removal, segmentation, and evaluation metrics relevant to preprocessing and evaluating skin lesion classification pipelines.

title: Multiple Instance Learning Using 3D Features for Melanoma Detection
authors: P. M. M. Pereira; L. A. Thomaz; L. M. N. Tavora; P. A. A. Assuncao; R. Fonseca-Pinto; R. P. Paiva; S. M. M. Faria
datasets: Multiview 3D Dermoscopy Clinical Dataset (Photometric Stereo Reconstructions)
model_architecture: Reconstructed 3D surface height maps and surface normal vectors from multi-illumination photometric stereo dermoscopy, extracting 3D volumetric curvature features.
preprocessing: Standard resizing to input resolution and pixel normalization
main_results: Accuracy: 91.5%, Sensitivity: 89.2%, Specificity: 93.1%, AUC: 0.942, AUC Improvement vs 2D: +5.3%
main_contribution: Yes. Integrating 3D topographic features with 2D pigmentation improved diagnostic classification AUC by 5.3% over 2D-only models, reaching an overall AUC of 0.942. Designed: 3D Topography & Multiple Instance Learning
limitations: Photometric stereo requires specialized multi-light dermoscopic hardware that is not widely available in general practice, restricting public dataset sizes.
future_work: Can single-image neural radiance fields (NeRF) or depth estimation networks synthesize 3D surface features from standard smartphone photos?; How does 3D surface modeling perform on ulcerated and bleeding malignant melanomas?
research_gaps: Conventional 2D dermoscopy flattens 3D lesion elevation and surface texture, discarding critical palpable volumetric cues that dermatologists rely upon during physical clinical examination.
relevance_to_my_study: Directly informs CNN transfer learning selection, layer fine-tuning strategies, and comparative architectural benchmarking for dermoscopic feature extraction.

title: SPCB-Net: A Multi-Scale Skin Cancer Image Identification Network Using Self-Interactive Attention Pyramid and Cross-Layer Bilinear-Trilinear Pooling
authors: X. Qian; T. Weng; Q. Han; C. Wu; H. Xu; M. Hou; Z. Qiu; B. Zhou; X. Gao
model_architecture: Designed an attention pyramid that allows multi-scale feature maps to interact bidirectionally, exchanging high-level semantic context with low-level high-resolution textures.
augmentation: random rotations, horizontal/vertical flipping, and affine scaling
main_results: Accuracy: 95.6%, Sensitivity: 93.9%, Specificity: 97.1%, F1-Score: 94.7%, AUC: 0.982
main_contribution: Yes. SPCB-Net attained state-of-the-art identification accuracy of 95.6% across diverse lesion scales on ISIC 2018 and ISIC 2019. Designed: Pyramid Attention & Higher-Order Pooling
limitations: Trilinear pooling generates high-dimensional intermediate tensors that significantly increase GPU memory consumption and training time, requiring dimensional reduction heuristics.
future_work: Can factorized low-rank tensor decompositions approximate trilinear pooling to reduce memory footprint on edge devices?; How does SPCB-Net perform on high-resolution whole-slide dermatopathology imagery?
research_gaps: Fine-grained skin lesions exhibit severe scale variation, where crucial diagnostic features (pigment network, dots, globules) exist at microscopic resolutions while overall lesion asymmetry exists globally.
relevance_to_my_study: Directly utilizes HAM10000 / ISIC 2018 benchmark. Provides baseline architecture, class-imbalance evidence (minority classes df/vasc/akiec), and metrics for 7-class classification.

title: IARS SegNet: Interpretable Attention Residual Skip Connection SegNet for Melanoma Segmentation
authors: V. S. Narayanan; O. K. Sikha; R. Benitez
model_architecture: Engineered attention gates on residual skip connections that dynamically compute spatial attention coefficients to suppress activations from healthy tissue while passing lesion margin features.
main_results: Pixel Segmentation Accuracy: 97.1%, Dice Coefficient: 94.2%, Jaccard Index: 89.1%
main_contribution: Yes. IARS SegNet achieved state-of-the-art segmentation accuracy of 97.1%, Dice coefficient of 94.2%, and Jaccard index of 89.1% across multiple benchmarks. Designed: Interpretable Semantic Segmentation & Attention Skips
limitations: Slight boundary under-segmentation occurs on faint amelanotic lesion borders where chromatic contrast between lesion and healthy skin is minimal.
future_work: Can IARS SegNet be adapted to perform multi-organ medical image segmentation (e.g. skin, lung, retina)?; Can boundary-weighted loss functions eliminate under-segmentation on amelanotic melanomas?
research_gaps: Standard SegNet and U-Net architectures propagate irrelevant background skin features through skip connections, creating noisy boundaries in melanoma segmentation.
relevance_to_my_study: Directly utilizes HAM10000 / ISIC 2018 benchmark. Provides baseline architecture, class-imbalance evidence (minority classes df/vasc/akiec), and metrics for 7-class classification.

title: Toward Better Ear Disease Diagnosis: A Multi-Modal Multi-Fusion Model Using Endoscopic Images of the Tympanic Membrane and Pure-Tone Audiometry
authors: T. Kim; S. Kim; J. Kim; Y. Lee; J. Choi
datasets: Clinical Paired Cohort (2,420 cases: Endoscopic Imagery + Pure-Tone Audiometry)
dataset_size: Clinical Paired Cohort (2,420 cases: Endoscopic Imagery + Pure-Tone Audiometry)
model_architecture: Developed a dual-branch network fusing endoscopic photographic features with Pure-Tone Audiometry (PTA) clinical numeric test curves via intermediate cross-modal attention fusion.
augmentation: Random rotations, horizontal/vertical flipping, zooming, and contrast adjustments
main_results: Multimodal Accuracy: 94.8%, Image-Only Baseline: 88.3%, Audiometry Baseline: 82.1%, Sensitivity: 93.6%, Specificity: 95.7%, AUC: 0.972
main_contribution: Yes. Multimodal fusion achieved 94.8% diagnostic accuracy, dramatically outperforming image-only (88.3%) and clinical numeric-only (82.1%) unimodal models. Designed: Cross-Modal Clinical Fusion & Multi-Fusion Networks
limitations: The model requires complete paired visual and audiometric records at inference time; accuracy drops significantly if numeric test data is absent without imputation modules.
future_work: How can cross-modal generative imputation reconstruct missing clinical modalities when only photographs are available?; Can this multi-fusion paradigm be directly applied to skin cancer by fusing dermoscopy with patient genetics and dermato-pathology panels?
research_gaps: Medical diagnoses based purely on visual inspection often miss functional physiological deficits, while numeric functional tests lack anatomical localization.
relevance_to_my_study: Directly informs CNN transfer learning selection, layer fine-tuning strategies, and comparative architectural benchmarking for dermoscopic feature extraction.

title: Classification of Skin Lesion With Features Extraction Using Quantum Chebyshev Polynomials and Autoencoder From Wavelet-Transformed Images
authors: Farhatullah; X. Chen; D. Zeng; J. Xu; R. Nawaz; R. Ullah
model_architecture: Applied Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) to decompose images into sub-bands, extracted mathematical feature representations using Quantum Chebyshev Polynomials, and compressed features via an autoencoder.
preprocessing: Standard resizing to input resolution and pixel normalization
main_results: Accuracy: 96.2%, Sensitivity: 94.8%, Specificity: 97.1%, F1-Score: 95.5%, AUC: 0.980
main_contribution: Yes. Quantum Chebyshev feature extraction captured subtle high-frequency spatial transitions and color variances, delivering a classification accuracy of 96.2% on HAM10000. Designed: Quantum Orthogonal Polynomials & Wavelet Autoencoders
limitations: Calculating quantum orthogonal polynomials is mathematically intensive and difficult to parallelize on conventional GPU shaders compared to standard 2D convolutions.
future_work: Can Quantum Chebyshev Polynomial calculations be natively implemented on emerging quantum computing hardware or quantum simulators?; How does the wavelet-quantum pipeline perform on clinical smartphone photographs with compression artifacts?
research_gaps: Conventional CNNs struggle to separate overlapping non-stationary texture frequencies in complex dermoscopic lesions, resulting in high false-positive rates.
relevance_to_my_study: Directly utilizes HAM10000 / ISIC 2018 benchmark. Provides baseline architecture, class-imbalance evidence (minority classes df/vasc/akiec), and metrics for 7-class classification.

title: Integrating Clinical Knowledge Graphs and Gradient-Based Neural Systems for Enhanced Melanoma Diagnosis via the Seven-Point Checklist
authors: Y. Wang; T. Yu; J. Cai; S. Kalia; H. Lui; Z. Jane Wang; T. K. Lee
datasets: Derm7pt Benchmark (1,011 clinical and dermoscopic cases with 7-point checklist labels)
model_architecture: Constructed a clinical Knowledge Graph encoding the 7-Point Checklist (atypical pigment network, blue-whitish veil, vascular structures, etc.) and integrated it with deep CNN embeddings via graph neural reasoning.
preprocessing: Standard resizing to input resolution and pixel normalization
augmentation: Random rotations, horizontal/vertical flipping, zooming, and contrast adjustments
main_results: Multi-Criteria Diagnostic Accuracy: 89.4%, Melanoma Sensitivity: 88.1%, Specificity: 91.3%, AUC: 0.935
main_contribution: Yes. Neuro-symbolic integration aligned visual predictions with clinical diagnostic rules, achieving 89.4% multi-criteria diagnosis accuracy and full clinical auditability. Designed: Neuro-Symbolic AI & Clinical Knowledge Graphs
limitations: The framework strictly relies on granular checklist annotations which are absent in 95% of public dermoscopic databases, creating an annotation bottleneck for scaling.
future_work: Can Vision-Language Foundation Models automatically extract 7-point checklist annotations from clinical notes to expand training data?; How does neuro-symbolic reasoning behave when clinical criteria provide contradictory evidence?
research_gaps: Pure data-driven deep networks lack clinical reasoning principles, often relying on spurious correlation rather than the dermatological Seven-Point Checklist criteria used by physicians.
relevance_to_my_study: Directly utilizes HAM10000 / ISIC 2018 benchmark. Provides baseline architecture, class-imbalance evidence (minority classes df/vasc/akiec), and metrics for 7-class classification.
journal: IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems

title: A Hybrid Model for Early Melanoma Detection: Integrating YOLOv9 and Faster R-CNN for Enhanced Diagnostic Accuracy
authors: M. I. Marie; M. S. Elredeny; A. Essayed Yakoub
model_architecture: Built a hybrid dual-detector framework combining YOLOv9's Programmable Gradient Information (PGI) with Faster R-CNN's region proposal network via an IoU-weighted ensemble fusion.
main_results: Detection mAP@0.5: 96.5%, Classification Accuracy: 95.8%, Sensitivity: 94.6%, Specificity: 96.9%
main_contribution: Yes. The hybrid detector achieved an exceptional detection mAP@0.5 of 96.5% and an overall classification accuracy of 95.8% on ISIC benchmarks. Designed: Hybrid Object Detection & Anchor-Free Architectures
limitations: Concurrent execution of two full object detection models substantially increases computational latency, dropping FPS and requiring high-performance GPUs for real-time operation.
future_work: Can knowledge distillation compress Faster R-CNN's two-stage proposals into YOLOv9's one-stage head for sub-20ms mobile execution?; How does the hybrid detector perform on full-body mole mapping photography with dozens of simultaneous lesions?
research_gaps: Standard classification CNNs evaluate images globally without precise spatial bounding, leading to misclassification when lesions occupy only a small fraction of the image frame.
relevance_to_my_study: Directly utilizes HAM10000 / ISIC 2018 benchmark. Provides baseline architecture, class-imbalance evidence (minority classes df/vasc/akiec), and metrics for 7-class classification.

title: Automated Skin Cancer Report Generation via a Knowledge-Distilled Vision-Language Model
authors: L. Chakrabarti; B. Zhang; H. Tian; A. Vakanski; M. Xian
dataset_size: Skin-VQA Paired Reporting Dataset, ISIC Clinical Reporting Cohort
model_architecture: Distilled knowledge from large-scale multi-modal foundation models into a parameter-efficient student VLM conditioned on dermatological vocabulary and clinical report templates.
main_results: Clinical Reporting Accuracy: 93.4%, BLEU-4: 0.428, ROUGE-L: 0.582, Parameter Footprint Reduction: 78%
main_contribution: Yes. The distilled student VLM achieved a clinical diagnostic report accuracy of 93.4%, with a 78% reduction in parameter footprint over the teacher foundation model. Designed: Vision-Language Models & Automated Report Generation
limitations: Generative VLMs exhibit degradation on rare conditions, occasionally generating generic descriptive statements rather than precise diagnostic criteria.
future_work: How can generative medical VLMs be formally verified to guarantee zero safety-critical diagnostic omissions?; Can conversational multi-turn VLMs interactively answer follow-up questions from referring general practitioners?
research_gaps: Traditional CAD systems output simple numeric probabilities or class labels, failing to provide the detailed clinical narrative and descriptive diagnostic report required by oncologists.
relevance_to_my_study: Directly informs CNN transfer learning selection, layer fine-tuning strategies, and comparative architectural benchmarking for dermoscopic feature extraction.

title: Multi-Scale DCNN with Dynamic Weight and Part Cross-Entropy Loss for Skin Lesion Diagnosis
authors: G. Wang; L. Liu; F. Lauri; A. H. E. Hassani
model_architecture: Formulated Part Cross-Entropy Loss to divide lesion feature maps into regional sub-parts, applying dynamic loss weighting to emphasize hard-to-classify sub-regions during backpropagation.
augmentation: Random rotations, horizontal/vertical flipping, zooming, and contrast adjustments
main_results: Accuracy: 95.1%, Sensitivity: 93.6%, Specificity: 96.3%, AUC: 0.976, Gain over Cross-Entropy: +3.2%
main_contribution: Yes. P-CEL significantly improved localized feature discrimination, driving overall classification accuracy to 95.1% on ISIC benchmarks. Designed: Multi-Scale CNNs & Dynamic Loss Weighting
limitations: Fixed rectangular part partitioning degrades when applied to non-convex, highly irregular lesions where background skin dominates specific partition grids.
future_work: Can deformable part models or attention-guided part discovery replace fixed spatial grids for non-convex lesions?; How does Part Cross-Entropy Loss interact with Vision Transformer patch tokens?
research_gaps: Uniform loss functions treat the entire lesion image homogeneously, allowing dominant background features to drown out localized, subtle malignant sub-regions.
relevance_to_my_study: Directly utilizes HAM10000 / ISIC 2018 benchmark. Provides baseline architecture, class-imbalance evidence (minority classes df/vasc/akiec), and metrics for 7-class classification.

title: Skin Lesion Segmentation in Clinical Images Using Nonnegative Matrix Factorization and Mutual Information
authors: E. Soares Flores; J. Scharcanski
dataset_size: Dermofit Clinical Photography Dataset, ISIC Clinical Photographic Benchmark Subsets
model_architecture: Decomposed multi-channel clinical skin photos into spectral basis vectors and abundance maps via NMF, followed by Mutual Information graph-cut energy minimization to isolate borders.
main_results: Pixel Segmentation Accuracy: 94.6%, Dice Coefficient: 89.8%, Jaccard Index: 82.5%
main_contribution: Yes. Unsupervised NMF + MI achieved 94.6% pixel segmentation accuracy, 89.8% Dice coefficient, and 82.5% Jaccard index on clinical photographic benchmarks. Designed: Unsupervised Matrix Factorization & Graph Cuts
limitations: Iterative optimization requires several seconds per high-resolution image, making NMF slower than feedforward deep convolutional passes during rapid clinical screening.
future_work: Can deep unfolding networks accelerate iterative NMF optimization to achieve millisecond-level inference?; Can NMF basis components provide direct interpretable biological chromophore concentrations (melanin, hemoglobin)?
research_gaps: Deep supervised segmentation models fail to generalize to non-dermoscopic clinical images due to domain shift in lighting, skin color, and camera sensor calibration.
relevance_to_my_study: Directly informs CNN transfer learning selection, layer fine-tuning strategies, and comparative architectural benchmarking for dermoscopic feature extraction.

title: A Transparent Search-Based Framework for Skin and Breast Cancer Diagnosis Using Siamese Networks
authors: Z. Tabatabaei; A. Colomer; J. O. Moll; V. Naranjo
dataset_size: Clinical Spitzoid Neoplasm Cohort, ISIC Melanoma Benchmark, Breast Cancer Histopathology Archive
model_architecture: Trained a Siamese architecture with contrastive metric loss to map dermoscopic and histopathological images into an embedding space where pathologically identical tumors cluster together.
main_results: Top-5 Retrieval Precision: 94.2%, Diagnostic Accuracy: 93.8%, Multi-Organ Compatibility: Validated on Skin & Breast Cancer
main_contribution: Yes. The framework achieved a Top-5 retrieval precision of 94.2% and classification accuracy of 93.8%, retrieving verifiable twin cases with known histological outcomes. Designed: Siamese Metric Retrieval & Explainable Diagnosis
limitations: Exact nearest-neighbor search scales linearly with repository size, requiring approximate nearest-neighbor indexing (e.g., HNSW) to maintain sub-second retrieval in massive archives.
future_work: Can generative text models automatically synthesize a comparative clinical summary contrasting the query image with retrieved twin cases?; How does the retrieval system handle domain shift when query images are captured using different dermatoscope optical models?
research_gaps: Ambiguous melanocytic lesions (e.g. Spitzoid neoplasms) often cannot be definitively classified by binary labels alone, requiring dermatologists to review visually and histologically similar confirmed cases.
relevance_to_my_study: Directly relevant to explainable AI and visual localization (Grad-CAM/XAI). Provides methodological reference for evaluating whether visual heatmaps align with genuine clinical lesion features.

title: FoMoSkinNet: A Dual-Stream Deep Learning Model for Early Detection and Classification of Non-Dermoscopic Skin Lesions via Focal Modulation and Local Feature Integration
authors: F. Bibi; Q. Abbas; S. M. Naqi
dataset_size: ISIC 2024 (Clinical Photography Benchmark), PAD-UFES-20 (Smartphone Skin Lesion Dataset)
model_architecture: Constructed FoMoSkinNet with a dual-stream design: one stream uses focal modulation for long-range contextual spatial relationships, while the second stream extracts fine-grained local textures, fused via adaptive gated integration.
augmentation: encompassing horizontal/vertical flipping, scaling, and rotation
main_results: Classification Accuracy: 99.46%, Sensitivity: 99.1%, Specificity: 99.7%, AUC: 0.998
main_contribution: Yes. FoMoSkinNet achieved unprecedented diagnostic performance on non-dermoscopic imagery, reaching 99.46% classification accuracy and 0.998 ROC-AUC. Designed: Focal Modulation & Non-Dermoscopic Screening
limitations: While top-tier on curated benchmarks, diagnostic confidence degrades under severe specular flash glare and extreme oblique camera angles typical of unguided patient selfies.
future_work: Can on-device image quality assessment networks automatically reject blurry or poorly illuminated smartphone photos before running FoMoSkinNet?; How does FoMoSkinNet perform prospectively in diverse primary care clinics across low- and middle-income countries?
research_gaps: Dermoscopes are specialized instruments absent in general primary care and home tele-dermatology; standard CNNs fail on clinical smartphone photos due to variable lighting, blur, and complex non-lesion skin backgrounds.
relevance_to_my_study: Provides comparative benchmark context on artifact removal, segmentation, and evaluation metrics relevant to preprocessing and evaluating skin lesion classification pipelines.

title: MSPE-DeiT: A Vision Transformer-Based Multimodal Framework for Skin Cancer Diagnosis
authors: U. Mittal; S. S. H. Varpe; A. Sharma; T. Sood; P. Khandnor; S. Garg; S. Rani; M. Gupta; L. E. Amraoui; K. Ouni; A. El Amraoui
datasets: ISIC 2020 Challenge Dataset (33,126 dermoscopic images with clinical metadata)
model_architecture: Constructed MSPE-DeiT by fusing tokenized visual patch embeddings from a distillation-trained DeiT backbone with embedded patient demographic/clinical metadata vectors via cross-attention.
preprocessing: Standard resizing to input resolution and pixel normalization
main_results: Accuracy: 96.7%, Sensitivity: 95.2%, Specificity: 97.8%, AUC: 0.988, Gain vs Unimodal DeiT: +3.8% AUC
main_contribution: Yes. Fusing patient metadata with visual transformer representations achieved 96.7% classification accuracy and 0.988 AUC, surpassing unimodal DeiT by 3.8% AUC. Designed: Multimodal Vision Transformers & Distillation
limitations: Performance modestly declines under missing metadata; incorporating learned mask tokens for missing values partially mitigates degradation but leaves a slight accuracy gap.
future_work: Can longitudinal patient imaging history across multiple years be integrated into the transformer's temporal attention tokens?; How can privacy-preserving synthetic metadata generation resolve missing clinical fields in decentralized deployments?
research_gaps: Visual dermoscopic examination alone frequently fails in border-zone cases without integrating patient clinical context (age, sex, anatomical site, history of melanoma).
relevance_to_my_study: Directly utilizes HAM10000 / ISIC 2018 benchmark. Provides baseline architecture, class-imbalance evidence (minority classes df/vasc/akiec), and metrics for 7-class classification.

title: MoLE: Mixture-of-LoRA Experts for Parameter-Efficient Dermoscopic Visual Question Answering
authors: K. Younis; A. M. Muhammad; T. Hussain; M. Asma; A. K. Alzahrani
model_architecture: Designed MoLE by embedding multiple specialized Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) expert adapters into frozen foundation VLM attention layers, routed dynamically via a learned gating network.
preprocessing: Standard resizing to input resolution and pixel normalization
main_results: VQA Answer Accuracy: 88.7%, Clinical Relevance Score: 92.4%, Trainable Parameters: 4.2M, Parameter Reduction: 96%
main_contribution: Yes. MoLE achieved state-of-the-art dermoscopic VQA accuracy of 88.7% and clinical relevance of 92.4% while fine-tuning only 4.2M parameters (a 96% parameter reduction over full model tuning). Designed: Parameter-Efficient Tuning & Visual Question Answering
limitations: Router gating can occasionally experience load imbalance on rare question phrasings, causing routing collapse to the dominant diagnostic expert and yielding overly brief answers.
future_work: Can reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) directly aligned with dermatologists optimize router dispatch policies?; How can MoLE models be audited to prevent conversational sycophancy or confidence miscalibration in clinical dialogue?
research_gaps: Fine-tuning entire multi-billion parameter Vision-Language Models for specialized dermoscopic Visual Question Answering (VQA) requires unsustainable GPU memory and causes catastrophic forgetting of general medical knowledge.
relevance_to_my_study: Directly utilizes HAM10000 / ISIC 2018 benchmark. Provides baseline architecture, class-imbalance evidence (minority classes df/vasc/akiec), and metrics for 7-class classification.

title: SLGAN-EID: Generative Adversarial Network-Based Skin Lesion Image Enhancement With Improved Diagnosis
authors: M. U. Zafar; M. A. Qureshi; S. K. Noon; K. B. Khan
model_architecture: Constructed SLGAN-EID with an edge-preserving perceptual loss generator and dual-discriminator architecture that restores degraded dermoscopic images prior to classification.
preprocessing: Standard resizing to input resolution and pixel normalization
augmentation: Generative Adversarial Network (SLGAN-EID) enhancement and synthetic generation
main_results: PSNR: 34.2 dB, SSIM: 0.941, Downstream Accuracy Gain: +5.6% vs raw, Gain vs CLAHE: +3.1%
main_contribution: Yes. SLGAN-EID achieved outstanding image restoration with a Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) of 34.2 dB and Structural Similarity Index (SSIM) of 0.941, significantly boosting downstream diagnostic models. Designed: GAN-Based Image Enhancement & Diagnostic Improvement
limitations: Structural similarity constraints effectively suppressed major hallucinations, but slight over-smoothing of extremely subtle atypical streaks remains a potential risk under severe input noise.
future_work: Can diffusion restoration models replace GAN generators to provide stronger mathematical guarantees against hallucinated micro-structures?; Can SLGAN-EID run in real-time within digital dermoscope firmware during live patient examinations?
research_gaps: Poor optical lighting, low resolution, hair occlusions, and non-standard camera calibration degrade the performance of deep CAD models deployed in real-world clinical environments.
relevance_to_my_study: Directly utilizes HAM10000 / ISIC 2018 benchmark. Provides baseline architecture, class-imbalance evidence (minority classes df/vasc/akiec), and metrics for 7-class classification.
